transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We're here for the readiness review on the real-time collaboration service ahead of Monday's 09:00 UTC production launch. As I understand it, the service passed its staging tests — functional, failover, and basic load — and the draft launch plan has a 10% initial rollout, up to 10,000 concurrent connections, the default 5-second retry interval, primary production region storage, and 90-day transcript retention. Before I finalize and record the binding policy, I'd like to hear from each of you — backend engineering, reliability, privacy, and customer success — on whether you see any blockers or concerns. Who'd like to start?

transcript.text: I need to raise a concern before we finalize. While investigating an unrelated mobile performance report this afternoon, I confirmed that mobile clients resume from background in bursts and currently retry every 5 seconds, which can create a reconnect storm. The rollout policy should set the retry interval to exactly 30 seconds instead of the default 5-second interval in the draft plan. I have not yet filed the client-library ticket for this.

transcript.text: I need to flag a capacity concern. About 20 minutes ago I completed a production-traffic replay and confirmed that the collaboration cluster's safe connection ceiling for Monday is exactly 6,000 concurrent connections — not the 10,000 in the draft plan. The autoscaling limit hasn't been updated yet because the replay results are still being attached to the capacity worksheet. We should lower the concurrent connection cap to 6,000 before finalizing.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a privacy blocker. I completed a privacy review this morning and confirmed two requirements that conflict with the draft launch plan: first, collaboration content for EU accounts must remain in the EU processing region — the draft plan only specifies primary production region storage, which won't satisfy this; second, session transcripts must be deleted after exactly 30 days, not the 90 days in the draft plan. I haven't opened the compliance ticket yet because legal was still reviewing the wording, but these are hard requirements that must be addressed before we finalize.

transcript.text: I need to raise a customer-success blocker. I reconciled the customer-success rollout spreadsheet about an hour ago and confirmed that six accounts — acct-204, acct-219, acct-233, acct-241, acct-278, and acct-301 — have administrator opt-out commitments until their enablement sessions are complete. These six accounts must be excluded from Monday's 10% initial rollout. I have not yet updated the launch checklist to reflect this exclusion.
